blocks.text: At 11:40 one night in September, Muzna had 74 unread chats and one idea: hire someone. A full-time hire at the national minimum wage costs about OMR 4,466 in the first year, and that is before the hours you spend training them. So before you decide whether to hire or automate, find out which of those 74 messages actually needed a person.

segments.text: Muzna is a composite example, built from owners like her. She runs an abaya and kaftan boutique in Al Mouj with a team of three: herself, a tailor, and her cousin at weekends. Most enquiries come in on WhatsApp, then Instagram, then the website.

Tourist season has started, so the chats now come in English as well as Arabic, and often late. A typical one is a voice note, "السلام عليكم، الكفتان الأخضر موجود ميديم؟", followed by a text: "delivery to Seeb kam?" Each one takes a minute to answer. Seventy of them take the whole evening.
So she priced the obvious fix. When she later sorted the chats themselves, the maths changed. More on that further down.

segments.text: An expatriate hire may take a lower salary. But work permit and visa fees, a medical test and often housing come on top, so add up the full cost before you assume it is cheaper.

blocks.text: A second employee works 40 hours a week, but your customers message you through all 168.

segments.text: The Labour Law limits normal work to eight hours a day and 40 a week. That is fair, and it is also the catch. Muzna's new hire would work roughly 10am to 6pm, which is when Muzna is already in the shop with her phone in reach.

Her worst hours come after 9pm. The shop is shut, tourists are planning tomorrow, and regular customers are scrolling Instagram after dinner. A second employee does nothing for those hours unless she pays for a second shift.
Before she interviewed anyone, Muzna scrolled back through one week of chats and sorted them into three piles. Her rough count (composite figures):

blocks.quote: I didn't need another pair of hands on my phone. I needed my phone to stop asking me the same question.

blocks.text: Second brain first, second employee later

segments.text: Muzna did both, in that order. In October she set up automatic replies on WhatsApp and the website for the repeat questions: prices, sizes, the location pin, delivery areas and hours. Anything about orders, complaints or custom work was saved as a lead for her to pick up in the morning. She chose Chatbot.OM because it understood voice notes in Omani Arabic, not just typed text.

In her composite first month, the midnight pile fell from about 70 unread chats to around 15 that really needed her. She still plans to hire, but for the shop floor during the winter rush. The job description no longer says "answer WhatsApp".

blocks.text: Hire people for the work only people can do, and let software take the questions you have already answered a hundred times.

segments.text: If your nights look like Muzna's, count your chats before you post a job advert. The count tells you which problem you actually have.

items.text: If more than half your chats are repeats, automate those first. It costs a fraction of a salary and it answers at 11pm.
If the real pressure is physical work (packing, fitting, serving, cleaning), hire. Software cannot fold a kaftan.
If both are true, automate first, then hire for the floor with a clearer job description.
Whatever you choose, ask where the chat data is stored. Oman's Personal Data Protection Law covers the names, numbers and messages any tool keeps for you.

blocks.title: Your ten-minute count
paragraphs: Open WhatsApp and scroll back through yesterday's chats. Make three tallies on paper: repeats, sales in progress, and only-me.
Circle every chat that arrived after 9pm. If more than half are repeats and many are circled, automation is your first move.
Then write down what you would actually give a new hire to do once the repeats are gone. If the list is short, you have just saved about OMR 372 a month.

items.q: Is OMR 325 the real monthly cost of an Omani hire?
items.a: It is the minimum wage. You also pay about 14.5 percent to the Social Protection Fund on top, and many owners pay more than the minimum to keep good staff.

items.q: Would an expatriate hire be cheaper?
items.a: The salary may be lower, but permit, visa and medical fees, and often housing, come on top. Work out the full first-year cost before you compare.

items.q: Will customers mind an automatic reply?
items.a: Someone asking about opening hours wants an answer, not a particular person. Make sure orders, complaints and anything unclear go to a human, and say so in the chat.

segments.text: A second employee is the right answer for work that needs hands and a smile. For the same ten questions arriving at midnight, a second brain costs less and never takes leave. Count your chats this week, and let the count decide.
